confirmed_facts.fact: Order ORD-2008 (wireless earbuds, Electronics, AED 499.00) was placed 27 Sep 2026 and delivered 29 Sep 2026; the return was requested 9 Oct 2026, 10.4 days after delivery.
Dispatch serial EB3-40882 matches the serial on the warehouse photo and the inspection record (exact comparison by code).
Warehouse inspection confirmed the fault: right earbud does not pair on test bench.
Parcel weight is consistent: dispatch 0.21 kg, pickup 0.22 kg, received 0.21 kg; the courier events are in order and the parcel was sealed at pickup.

findings.description: The order was placed before 1 Oct 2026 (Return v1 applies by order date) but the return was requested after 1 Oct 2026 (Return v2 applies by request date). Return v1 gives a 14-day window (inside at 10.4 days); Return v2 gives 7 days for electronics (outside). The two versions give different answers and no record settles which applies.

evidence.quote: Applies to:** orders placed from 1 January 2025 to 30 September 2026.
Applies to:** return requests made on or after 1 October 2026.

policy_references.quote: Customers may return any item within **14 days** of delivery, for any reason.
A manufacturing defect that appears within **12 months** of delivery is covered even after the return window has closed.
Two policy versions could apply and give different answers: escalate (Return policy owner decides).

findings.rationale: Two return policy versions could apply and give different answers on the return window (inside under Return v1, outside under Return v2 for electronics). The fault is confirmed at inspection and the serial and weight records are consistent. The Return policy owner should decide which version applies, and the defect and warranty route (Defect 1.1 and 1.3, repair or replacement) may also be relevant.
findings.uncertainty_note: The facts are well supported by records. The open point is only which policy version governs; the outcome (return refund, or warranty repair or replacement) depends on that decision.
